thesis: One Genie 4 session for the whole of Reunion (65 s): an Ethiopian sci-fi western. The opening frame turns the last shot of a classic western around: seen from inside a dark homestead, through the doorway, the men come home instead of one man walking away. Leone gives the beats (long held wides, a slow push in, faces and hands); Haile Gerima gives the ground (highland farm life, elders, earth, water carried by donkey). Each line of the poem is sent into the same session as a short text beat just before he says its key word.
seed_why: Made for this take with gemini-3-pro-image (prompt in full/seeds12west/prompt.txt), because Genie builds the shot from the picture. Candidate b of two: the darker doorway gives the western's silhouette frame, and the low sun lets the night in line 6 arrive.
world_lock: An Ethiopian science-fiction western in the Tigray highlands, near-future: stone farmhouses, flat-topped amba mesas and canyons, donkeys carrying yellow jerrycans of water, a silver fog-harvesting tower on a mesa. Everyone here is Black and Ethiopian. Shot like Sergio Leone (wide anamorphic landscapes, long silences, slow push-ins, faces and hands) crossed with Haile Gerima (real farm life, elders, earth, dignity, natural light).
seed:
PLACE. Late afternoon turning to sunset. We are inside a dark stone farmhouse, looking out through its rough doorway at a red-earth plain, amba mesas on the horizon, one sycamore tree on a ridge, a tall silver fog-harvesting tower with mesh sails on the right.

PEOPLE. Four Black Ethiopian men in their fifties, old friends coming home, walk toward the doorway through the dust leading grey donkeys loaded with yellow plastic jerrycans of water. The poet walks in front: close-cropped greying hair, short beard, black long-sleeved top, black trousers, a white cotton gabi shawl over one shoulder, a wooden staff. Beside him: a man in a rust-orange corduroy jacket with a grey tee; a bald man in a sky-blue shirt; a man in a green football jersey and a grey flat cap. Each has a white gabi shawl. In the dark foreground at the left of the doorway, an elderly Black Ethiopian woman in her seventies in a white cotton netela with an embroidered tibeb border stands with one hand on the doorframe, waiting for them.

WHAT HAPPENS. They come slowly, laughing, shoulders bumping, the donkeys' bells clinking, and stop in the yard about twenty paces from the door. They stay out there in the light, small in the doorway frame, for nearly the whole scene; only at the very end do they walk inside. The water sloshes in the jerrycans. The light goes from gold to copper to blue night over the minute.

CAMERA. Locked off on a tripod inside the house at standing height, looking out through the doorway. It never moves, never walks, never goes outside: one long patient frame, the doorway's black stone edges always around the bright land, like the last shot of a classic western.

LIGHT. Low sun behind them, long shadows toward us, dust glowing, deep brown skin with full tonal range, warm grade, fine grain.

SOUND. Wind, donkey bells, footsteps on stony earth, distant laughter. Leave room for one man's speaking voice.

cues.send: Far off in the sun the four men throw their heads back and laugh out loud; a donkey brays.
The elder woman in the white netela steps into the doorway light, her eyes squinting into the glare, her hand still on the stone.
The sky goes dark copper; a wall of dust rolls over the plain and blots out the sun behind the men.
Inside the house behind the doorway: a row of empty wooden chairs and a cold clay jebena coffee pot.
Each man lifts a small glass hourglass whose sand glows like burning embers in his hand.
Wind moves through the lone sycamore tree on the ridge; its leaves shine.
Out in the yard the four men stand in a line facing the house in a long silent standoff, then embrace.
Out in the yard one man rests his ear on his brother's chest.
Beyond them the hilltops and canyons of the mesas glow; blinding light flares from the silver fog tower.
Night falls fast: stars over the mesas, the fog tower glowing blue, a fire lit in front of the house.
Around the fire they laugh together while the elder woman pours coffee from the jebena.
A worn football is kicked across the dirt yard in the firelight; a donkey watches.
The men walk in through the doorway past the elder woman, home.

take_notes.12west-1125-0122: Take 1: the doorway frame held for the first 12 s, then the poet walked straight up to the camera and the W push at 30 s drove into his face (extreme close-ups to the end). Hourglasses, a small fire and the football landed; dusk, night and the dust storm did not. Take 2: no keys, men told to stop in the yard and stay there until the last line, camera locked off.
